Column guide: "value" is the latest survey value and "year" its survey year. "previous_value" and
"previous_year" are the survey before it, and "change" is value minus previous_value. A column ending in
"average" is the simple average of the latest values of the countries in that group. A column named after a country
is that country's latest value, and the column ending in "year" beside it is its survey year. A column
starting "gap vs" is value minus that comparator. "region_rank" is the country's position among
"region_countries" countries in its own region, where 1 is the highest value. "obstacle_rank" ranks the
biggest-obstacle indicators within the country, where 1 is the obstacle firms name most often. "flags" are
notes produced by simple rules. Empty cells mean no data.

TASK: Write exactly one point for each of these topics: Gender, Finance, Infrastructure and Climate. For each topic, choose its most interesting indicator, or a pair of indicators that tell a story together.

RULES:
- Use only numbers that appear in DATA, written exactly as they appear or rounded to a whole number.
  Do not calculate any new number.
- Describe what the data show. Do not claim causes.
- If a change looks too large to be plausible between two survey rounds, say in "verify" what should be
  checked. Otherwise set "verify" to an empty string.
- Plain English. Each "text" is at most 45 words. Do not put indicator codes in the text.

Return only JSON: a list of objects with the keys "headline" (at most 8 words), "text",
"indicators" (the list of indicator codes the point uses) and "verify".

checks.headline: Female leadership and employment shares have expanded
Access to finance constraints have worsened sharply
Frequent water shortages pose severe operational challenges

points_used.headline: Female leadership and employment shares have expanded
points_used.text: The share of firms with a woman top manager rose from 4.5% in 2015 to 16.4% in 2025, approaching the regional average of 17.8%. Additionally, women made up 38.2% of permanent full-time workers in 2025, up from 27.7% in 2015.
points_used.verify: Verify whether the share of firms with a woman top manager truly rose from 4.5% to 16.4% between survey rounds.

points_used.headline: Access to finance constraints have worsened sharply
points_used.text: In 2025, 56.8% of firms identified access to finance as a major or very severe constraint, up from 20.3% in 2015 and above the Sub-Saharan Africa average of 39.8%. Furthermore, 39.6% of firms are fully credit constrained.
points_used.verify: Verify whether the proportion of firms reporting access to finance as a major constraint more than doubled from 20.3% to 56.8%.

points_used.headline: Frequent water shortages pose severe operational challenges
points_used.text: In 2025, 52.4% of firms experienced water insufficiencies, well above the Sub-Saharan Africa average of 24.7%. Firms reported an average of 12.0 water insufficiencies in a typical month, compared to the regional benchmark of 7.3.
